newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish government welcomes Aer Lingus' 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Irish government welcomes Aer Lingus' 1996 results.

text.p: Irish transport minister Alan Dukes on Wednesday welcomed the announcement by Aer Lingus of its 1996 annual results.
The airline reported a 130 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profits to 40.9 million Irish pounds while operating profits rose by four percent to 41.8 million.

"The early 1990s were difficult for the global aviation industry and Aer Lingus, like many other airlines, was compelled to restructure its operations in order to meet the challenges posed by a constantly changing market," Dukes said in a statement.
"That these challenges have been successfully met to date is amply demonstrated by the 1996 results which mirror the turnaround shown in recent years."

But Dukes cautioned that the airline must continue to position itself to meet on-going competitive challenges and to build up profits to meet re-investment needs and to cope with the next downturn in its cyclical industry.

"It is for these reasons that the board of Aer Lingus was recently mandated to continue to operate to strict commercial criteria and to explore the possibility of entering into a strategic alliance," he said.
